name: RMP Electrical
seen: The logo is a black serif RMP monogram with a small blue lightning bolt through the M, next to the words RMP Electrical.
The page is warm cream, alternating with white bands, and one near-black band (the quote form) with a faint grain.
Three action colours sit side by side: a green WhatsApp button, a near-black Call button, and navy for labels, links and icons.

Headlines are large light serif with the last words in italic (Your local electricians. / Small jobs, done properly. / Real jobs. Real homes.). The same italic-ending pattern repeats on every section.
Cards, photos and buttons have generous rounded corners; buttons are pills; the service tiles use small icons in pale grey-blue squares.

The first screen shows a real person (a man in grey work clothes reading his phone beside an EV charger) with a floating card saying Phone on, 24 hours a day, and a badge naming Uxbridge, West London and Ryan Pumfrey.
Recent work is a grid of phone-style job photos (ceiling light, backlit mirror, outdoor lantern with EV charger, spotlights, consumer unit, LED strip). Quality varies and some look soft.
Home runs: hero, trust strip (24/7, qualified, free quotes), dark quote form, eight service tiles, recent work, how quoting works, about Ryan, reviews with owner replies.
A green Message Ryan button floats bottom-right on every screen; a cookie card covers the bottom-left.
The service page is a plain reading layout with a breadcrumb; no photo was visible in the screens captured.
check: The service page has an empty band of about 150 pixels between the intro line and the first paragraph. Cause unknown: it may be an image that did not load, or a scroll reveal.
The cookie card was left open, so it hides part of every screen. Nothing was clicked.
The site says every recent-work photo is from a real job. RMP should confirm that.
The reviews carry names and owner replies. Where they come from (Google or elsewhere) is not shown on the page.
The Areas page was not captured.

method: Screenshots taken with scripts/visual/capture.mjs and looked at by eye. Descriptions say what was visible on the screen. Font names, hex codes and image ownership were not read from code and are not claimed.
